Resolve a sibling helper next to this script.

    The package installs the GUI and its helpers side by side in
    ``/usr/bin``; a source checkout keeps them side by side in
    ``desktop/bin``. Resolving next to this file means a checkout runs
    its own helpers (so edits take effect immediately) instead of
    silently driving the packaged copy. Falls back to ``/usr/bin`` when
    no sibling exists.

Return `(label, active)` for the "Associazione" row.

    A bond record is not an association. When the phone dissociates — or simply
    goes away — the desktop keeps the record but has nothing left to talk to,
    so the row must not read green (observed 2026-09-24: the card said
    "Associato" while the phone was dissociated and phone unlock was dead).

Return `(label, active)` for the "Ultimo sblocco" row.

    A past unlock proves nothing while no phone is associated: keep the
    timestamp readable, but only colour the row green when the association is
    actually live.

Return the patched DMS lock tree, or None when no tree carries the hook.

    The fingerprint indicator used to be gated on a `pam_syauth.so` line inside
    the lock PAM stack. That line is gone for good: a DeskUnlock module in a
    stack that guards the login is how the operator ended up unable to get back
    in with the correct password — twice (2026-09-23). The phone unlock is out
    of band now: the lock screen calls `syauth unlock-request` on the operator's
    gesture. Every marker the patch writes must be present, so a half-applied
    adaptation (DMS moved an anchor) reads as broken instead of "Attivo".

True when the patch recorded that the running DMS loaded `tree`.

    DMS loads its extracted QML once and does not watch it, so a tree patched
    after DMS started is inert: the lock screen keeps the stock icon and never
    asks the phone. The patch writes `dms-lock-loaded` with the adapted tree
    name(s) right after it restarts DMS, and that marker — not the on-disk
    patch — is what says the running shell actually has the adaptation
    (2026-09-24).
True when the daemon saw a recent presence heartbeat from the phone.

Return `(ok, reason)` for the fingerprint/phone unlock row.

    The GUI used to show "Attivo" whenever the tree was patched on disk, even
    when DMS had loaded the unpatched copy, the runtime marker was missing, or
    the daemon was down. Every failure now names itself so the row is honest.

Return QProcess parameters that put the child in its own session.

    The pairing dialog launches a shell wrapper that in turn spawns the
    real ``syauth pair`` process. Without a private session, killing the
    wrapper leaves the real process orphaned. ``CreateNewSession`` makes
    the wrapper a session/process-group leader so
    :func:`terminate_process_tree` can signal the whole tree at once.

    Returns ``None`` when the Qt build predates ``UnixProcessParameters``
    (Qt < 6.6); callers then fall back to a plain ``start``.

SIGKILL the process group led by ``pid``.

    Pure ``os``; safe to call from a non-Qt worker thread. Never raises:
    a group that already exited, or a signal the kernel refused, is a
    no-op. Falls back to the bare pid when the process is not a group
    leader.

Reap ``process`` and every descendant it spawned.

    Reads the process-group id from ``process`` and delegates to
    :func:`kill_process_group`. Main-thread only (touches QProcess).

Return the language to use.

    `configured` is the operator's choice ("auto" or a supported code); `env`
    is the process environment. An unsupported or empty answer falls back to
    [DEFAULT_LANGUAGE] instead of to the desktop's locale, so a `de_DE` desktop
    reads a coherent English GUI rather than whatever mixed catalog happens to
    exist.

Bind the module-level `_` to `language`.

    English is the source language, so it maps to the identity: no catalog
    lookup and no failure mode when `/usr/share/locale` is empty.
